title: prepublish.mjs cannot spawn npm on Windows since the Bun 1.4.2 pin, so the tag-time qualification emits no receipt
description:
Found at tag time on the 0.12.0 release, and it is publication-blocking: no native-execution receipt is emitted, so nothing can be staged.

MEASURED: qualification run 36694113900 on the v0.12.0 tag. source-gates success; darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64 success; win32-x64 FAILURE; win32-arm64 FAILURE; candidate-bundle and native-execution-receipt both skipped. Both Windows legs fail at step 7, bun scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs, with package_contents_and_provenance passed, then root_pack FAILED and candidate_smoke_validation FAILED, both reporting "spawn npm.cmd EINVAL" and publicationBlocking: true. root_pack is the first gate that spawns npm, so every npm call in that script is dead on Windows.

ROOT CAUSE, isolated by elimination rather than assumed. prepublish.mjs maps npm to npm.cmd on win32 and handed it to execFile with no shell. A .cmd passed to spawn without a shell now fails EINVAL -- the hardening that followed CVE-2024-27980, which Bun aligned with in the 1.4.x line. What makes the attribution clean instead of a guess: the script, the gate list, the npm.cmd mapping and the Windows runner images (windows-2022, windows-11-arm) are all byte-identical to the v0.11.0 tag, whose qualification run 36285769701 completed SUCCESS on 2026-09-27. The only variable that differs between the two runs is the workflow bun-version: 1.3.14 then, 1.4.2 now.

So the pin move to Bun 1.4.2 (QCLI-411) is what surfaced this. The pin move is not itself wrong; a latent Windows bug in a qualification script was hiding behind the older runtime.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: adding the shell option is the unsafe shape (Node DEP0190 -- arguments are concatenated, not escaped) and it also breaks on any path containing a space, which is exactly the Windows temp path shape this script builds. The fix quotes every argument itself and hands a finished command line to cmd.exe with windowsVerbatimArguments, which is the pattern cross-spawn uses.

VERIFICATION CONSTRAINT, recorded because it shapes the fix: this host is darwin, so the Windows branch cannot be executed here. The helper is therefore a side-effect-free module taking the platform as a parameter, so the win32 argv shape is asserted from any host, and the real proof is the Windows legs of a dispatched matrix run.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The Windows legs of a six-platform dispatch run go green, named by run id and head SHA, with every leg reported individually
The POSIX legs of that same run stay green, so the fix did not regress the path that already worked
prepublish.mjs reaches npm on Windows without EINVAL, and does so without the shell option, which a test refuses by name
The win32 argument shape is asserted from a non-Windows host, so the fix is verifiable without a Windows runner
A path containing a space survives as one argument, which is the specific way the shell-option form fails
